steps: TIME-CRITICAL — activate stroke pathway, non-contrast CT immediately.
IV thrombolysis (alteplase/tenecteplase) if within window and no contraindication.
Mechanical thrombectomy for large-vessel occlusion up to 24 h in selected patients.
Aspirin 300 mg once haemorrhage excluded (delay 24 h after thrombolysis).
Admit to stroke unit; permissive hypertension, glucose/temperature control, swallow screen, early secondary prevention.

drugRefs.dose: 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg) — 10% as bolus, remainder over 60 min
drugRefs.why: Reperfuses ischaemic tissue within the licensed window (typically ≤4.5 h) once haemorrhage is excluded.

drugRefs.dose: 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) as a single IV bolus
drugRefs.why: Single-bolus thrombolytic alternative to alteplase, especially where thrombectomy is planned.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Ischemic Stroke
AHA/ASA Guidelines for the Early Management of Acute Ischemic Stroke
NICE NG128 — Stroke and Transient Ischaemic Attack in Over 16s

drugRefs.duration: for 2 weeks, then switch to long-term secondary-prevention antiplatelet
drugRefs.why: Reduces early recurrence; start once haemorrhage excluded and delay 24 h after thrombolysis.

confirm: Sudden focal neurological deficit; non-contrast CT to exclude haemorrhage, then confirm ischaemia. Establish last-known-well time.
